blocks.c: Come on. You knew. I knew. I had known since the tag said SORRY.

For the record, I did it properly. I told my brother I was going to be late. I put a wedge in the freight car door track so it could not close all the way. I took my phone, a torch, a radio, and the black log book under my arm, because rule one was the only rule I had.
I got in at 1:20 in the morning. I pressed the unnumbered button.
The wedge popped out of the track like a watermelon seed.

Now: the Merridew has two basements. B1 is loading and storage. B2 is plant — chillers, pumps, the sprinkler riser. Below B2 is dirt, and under the dirt is the water table, and under that is the actual planet.
The freight car ran for eleven seconds.

I have timed that car a hundred times. Floor to floor is four seconds. Eleven seconds is more than two floors and less than three, and it is exactly the amount of time in which a person can decide four separate times that this was a mistake.
I was looking at the lobby.

Not a lobby. The lobby. The Merridew's ground-floor lobby: terrazzo floor, the ficus that dies every eighteen months, the security desk, the brass letters over the elevators reading MERRIDEW TOWER 1974.
Except the ficus was alive and enormous.
Except the desk had no monitors on it.
Except through the front doors, where the street should have been, there was nothing at all. Not darkness. Nothing, in the way a screen is nothing when it is off.
And the log book, under my arm, had gone warm.
